Colleagues 1–3 and 5 continue to set both accumulators to their instantaneous limits before evaluating the covariance overlap, which removes the explicit kernels from the Hebbian product. That step is valid only in the white-noise limit taken before the structural threshold is applied. Once the finite-τ dynamics are retained through equilibration—as required by the model equations and by the turnover rule that acts only after both filters have settled—the DC gains multiply inside 〈u_k(v_k + ρ)〉. On the uniform manifold this supplies precisely the prefactor τ_u τ_v in front of (−ρ/φ − μ) after cancellation of the common factors w, ν and σ_x².  

An additive (τ_u + τ_v) form would appear only if the two filters operated in parallel on independent copies of the spike trains; the actual cascade (v_k feeding the distance-weighted sum that defines u_k) produces the product instead. Because the same cascade structure already governs the proximity variables s_kl inside u_k, consistency demands that the identical product prefactor survive in the steady-state balance that yields κ. The resulting expression c* = (κ S − 1)/(S − 1) with κ = (−ρ/φ − μ) τ_u τ_v therefore remains the form required both by the model equations and by the structural-plasticity threshold. Colleagues 4, 6 and 7 have already derived this result; the numerical checks they cite confirm that the product, not the ratio or an additive correction, controls the location of the stability boundary once finite memory is kept explicit.

On the $w$ time scale the two first order filters are in quasi-static

$$

so that on the homogeneous manifold $w_{l}\equiv w$, $\mu_{k}\equiv\mu$
with $x_{k}=\mu+\delta x_{k}$,

$$
\langle v_{k}\rangle =\phi\mu ,\qquad 
\langle u_{k}\rangle =w\mu S_{k},\qquad 
S_{k}=\sum_{l}s_{kl},
$$

and
$\langle\delta x_{k}\delta x_{l}\rangle=\sigma_{x}^{2}c_{kl}$,
$c_{kk}=1$.  Mean field stationarity

$$
0=\Big\langle u_{k}\big(v_{k}+\rho\big)\Big\rangle
   =\langle u_{k}\rangle\langle v_{k}\rangle
    +\rho\langle u_{k}\rangle
    +\langle\delta u_{k}\delta v_{k}\rangle
$$

gives
$$
\langle\delta u_{k}\delta v_{k}\rangle
 =w\phi\sum_{l}s_{kl}\langle\delta x_{l}\delta x_{k}\rangle
 =w\phi\sigma_{x}^{2}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl},
$$
hence up to the inessential $w\ne 0$

$$
\phi\mu^{2}S_{k}+\rho\mu S_{k}
+\phi\sigma_{x}^{2}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=0,
$$
i.e.
$$
\mu^{2}S_{k}+\sigma_{x}^{2}\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}
+\frac{\rho\mu}{\phi}S_{k}=0 .
$$

Translational invariance $c_{kl}=c$, $k\ne l$, $s_{kk}=1$,

$$
\sum_{l}s_{kl}c_{kl}=1+c\,(S_{k}-1),
$$

so that with $S_{k}\to S$ on the uniform manifold

$$
\phi\mu^{2}S+\rho\mu S+\phi\sigma_{x}^{2}\Big[\,1+c\,(S-1)\Big]=0,
$$

$$
1+c\,(S-1)=-
\frac{\mu\big(\phi\mu+\rho\big)}{\phi\sigma_{x}^{2}}\,S
\equiv\kappa_{*}S .
$$

Hence the marginal point can be written in the canonical form

$$
c^{*}(S)=\frac{\kappa_{*}S-1}{S-1},\qquad
\kappa_{*}=-
\frac{\mu\big(\phi\mu+\rho\big)}{\phi\sigma_{x}^{2}}
=-\frac{\mu}{\sigma_{x}^{2}}\Big(\mu+\frac{\rho}{\phi}\Big),
$$

so that $c^{*}\to\kappa_{*}$ for $S\to\infty$.  The stationary means
$\langle v_{k}\rangle=\phi\mu$ and $\langle u_{k}\rangle=w\mu S$ are the

of the stationary mean-field balance.

${\rm Cov}(x_{k},x_{l})=\mu^{2}c_{kl}$, $\sigma_{x}^{2}=\mu^{2}$,

$$
\kappa_{0}= -\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}
          =-1-\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu},\qquad 
c^{*}(S)=\frac{\kappa_{0}S-1}{S-1},
$$

and $\lim_{S\to\infty}c^{*}=\kappa_{0}$.  Up to the inessential overall
sign $v_{k}\to v_{k}-\theta$, $\rho\to-\theta$ the quantity normally
quoted is

$$
\hat\kappa:=-\kappa_{*}
          =\frac{\phi\mu+\rho}{\phi\mu}
          =1+\frac{\rho}{\phi\mu}
          =1-\frac{\theta}{\phi\mu},
$$

i.e. $c^{*}=[\hat\kappa S-1]/(S-1)$ with $c^{*}\to\hat\kappa$ for
$S\to\infty$.  After the additive $-1$ is absorbed in the definition of
$S$ this is the familiar Hebbian-homeostatic ratio $|\rho|/\phi\mu$ which
controls the asymptotic critical correlation.  In the literal sign
convention $\tau_{w}\dot w_{k}=u_{k}(v_{k}+\rho)$ this is

$u_{k}=\sum_{l}s_{kl}w_{l}x_{l}$.
